A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Progressive Tempering Sampler with Diffusion. All 23 pages, including Appendices A–D, equations, figures and tables, are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and molecular evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark measurements, alanine dipeptide experiments and supplementary evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same temperature guidance, sequential diffusion training, truncated importance resampling and local parallel-tempering refinement.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MoG/GMM-40, MW-32, LJ-55 and alanine dipeptide. Appendix D.1 retains the additional DW-4 and LJ-13 extrapolation tests, with no coverage changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baseline membership, including FAB, CMCD, DDS, iDEM, BNEM, DiKL and PT+DM. The extrapolation alternatives and the comparator subset in Table 8 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Metrics, temperature schedules, training budgets, sample counts and preprocessing remain identical in the main text and appendices. Appendix D.6 retains the separate LJ55 evaluation using 1,000 additional Langevin steps.

E4.justification: The guidance and importance-resampling ablations in Table 4, extrapolation comparisons in Appendix D.1, and molecular, sample-visualization and Langevin-refinement analyses in D.4–D.6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same multiple-seed and repeated-sampling uncertainty procedures, exclusion of undefined MW32 runs, and log-likelihood standard-error calculation. No statistical reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout, including Tables 1–4, 7 and 8. For example, PTSD's MW32 W2 remains 4.99 ± 0.07, with 5.3 × 10^6 target evaluations.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations remain unchanged, including the temperature-guidance derivation in Equations 9–11 and the appendix metric and likelihood formulas. No theoretical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about temperature guidance, progressive sampler training, sample quality and target-evaluation efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are retained, including LJ55 performance explanations, alanine mode-coverage tradeoffs, and limitations concerning wall-clock cost, sequential execution and temperature-schedule sensitivity.

D1.justification: Appendix C, Tables 5–6 and Appendix D.4 retain identical architecture, hyperparameter, processing and implementation information. The code-access statement and repository information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and Section 4 research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to neural samplers, MCMC integration and diffusion guidance.

P1.justification: v2 adds an author-order explanation about rock-paper-scissors to the equal-contribution footnote. Three cross-reference labels change from 'App.' to 'Sec.', and the version/date stamp updates. The narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded first-page author footnote causes local text reflow, and the margin version/date stamp changes. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–8 retain their graphics, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes small authorship-note, cross-reference and formatting edits. The methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
